children: EQT will buy Qiagen for $12 bln, whose kits trace diseases and help police solve crimes. It’s barely more than an offer shareholders rejected back in 2020. Yet the Swedish buyer will need to grow beyond current forecasts and crank up margins to get a decent return.
Full view will be published shortly.
Sweden's EQT will buy molecular testing company Qiagen for about €9.6 billion ($10.78 billion), the companies said on October 21.

Buyout firm EQT offered €46.50 ($52.22) a share for Qiagen, representing an 8.6% premium to its last close. Affiliates of the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board are also participating in the offer.
The deal, which values Qiagen at about $12.1 billion including about $1.1 billion in net debt, is expected to close in mid-2027. EQT has secured equity and debt financing to fund the offer.
Qiagen said it was suspending its full-year 2026 outlook pending the deal. It reported preliminary third-quarter net sales of $548 million and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.65.
Qiagen shares were trading at €45.12 ($50.70) by 0833 GMT on October 22.
